stories.headline: Could aliens ever visit Earth? An aerospace scientist unpacks the challenges of interstellar spaceflight
stories.summary: An aerospace scientist has discussed the challenges of interstellar spaceflight, stating that while no single law of physics prohibits an interstellar voyage to Earth, the combined effects of extreme engineering requirements may render it physically infeasible. The speed of light is a structural limit, making interstellar travel impossible due to the rocket equation. Advanced civilizations may master stellar energy but decide that crossing interstellar space is not worth the cost. Alternatively, if they are advanced enough to traverse interstellar distances, they may also be able to remain hidden. The question of whether aliens could visit Earth without being detected is both philosophical and scientific, challenging assumptions about knowledge, perception, and reality. The Fermi paradox remains unanswered, with scientists like Dr. Robin Corbett suggesting that extraterrestrials may find space travel banal or not worth the effort.

stories.headline: I turned off GPU shared memory in BIOS and my PC finally felt like 16GB again
stories.summary: A user discovered that disabling GPU shared memory in their BIOS settings significantly improved their PC's performance, making it feel like it had 16GB of RAM again. This is because the system reserves a portion of RAM for the integrated GPU (iGPU), even when a discrete GPU is used. Disabling this setting frees up the reserved RAM for general use. Users with 16GB of RAM or less are likely to notice a greater impact from disabling iGPU memory reservation. This setting can be changed in the BIOS, and decreasing shared GPU memory can help improve system performance. The effect is more noticeable for those with lower RAM configurations or who are using graphics cards with limited VRAM, such as 6GB or 8GB models. This tweak can help optimize system resources and improve overall performance.

stories.headline: PS5's Destruction AllStars Delisted, Servers Officially Disabled Without Notice
stories.summary: Destruction AllStars, a multiplayer vehicular arena combat game, has been delisted from the PS Store without prior notice. The game's servers have been offline since 2024, and Sony has now officially acknowledged the shutdown. Despite initial support promises, the game experienced a steep player decline, leading to server issues since May 2024. As a result, PlayStation has disabled the game's multiplayer services, effective immediately. The game was one of the first exclusive titles for the PlayStation 5 and has seen a significant decline in player base. Refunds are not mentioned for current owners, but the game is no longer available for purchase. The shutdown marks the end of the game's live service, with no further updates or support planned. The delisting and server shutdown are now official, bringing an end to the game's online multiplayer functionality.

stories.headline: GCL Announces the Global Console and PC Version 1.0 Release of 'Realm of Ink'
stories.summary: GCL Global Holdings has launched 'Realm of Ink' Version 1.0 worldwide on PC and major consoles. The game's release marks its exit from Early Access and is a significant milestone for GCL and its publishing team at 4Divinity. According to Sebastian Toke, Group CEO at GCL, the launch is an exciting milestone for the company. The release reinforces GCL's strategy of promoting Asian-developed intellectual properties on global gaming platforms. This launch follows recent investments and publishing agreements, including a $10 million strategic investment from ADATA. 'Realm of Ink' is now available globally as of May 26, 2026, across PC and major consoles, signaling a new phase in the game's development and GCL's expansion into the global gaming market. The company aims to further establish itself as a key player in the industry.

stories.headline: Arsenal aiming to join list of unbeaten Champions League winners Nine teams have lifted the trophy without suffering defeat across the whole season in the Champions League era.
stories.summary: Arsenal is aiming to join the list of unbeaten Champions League winners, having maintained an unbeaten record across all 14 of their European matches this season. They will face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final on May 30 in Budapest. If they win, they will become the first team to win the competition without a defeat under the current 15-game format. Nine teams have previously lifted the trophy without suffering a defeat across the whole season in the Champions League era. Arsenal's disciplined defending, attacking quality, and consistency have impressed throughout the competition. A win would secure the club's first-ever Champions League title and earn them a place in the exclusive list of unbeaten winners, commanding historic respect in European football. The Gunners are one step away from achieving this feat under manager Arteta.

stories.headline: Man City 'ahead of' Man Utd for 'record' transfer for three key reasons A new report has confirmed that Manchester City are 'ahead of' Manchester United in the race to sign Elliot Anderson for three reasons.
stories.summary: Manchester City are leading the race to sign Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, ahead of rivals Manchester United. Anderson is leaning towards a move to Etihad Stadium, with a growing expectation that he will leave the City Ground this summer. Manchester City hope to sign him before the World Cup, but are currently £25m short of Nottingham Forest's valuation. There are three key reasons why Manchester City are ahead in the transfer race. Transfer expert Fabrizio Romano has suggested that Manchester City may not be prepared to meet Nottingham Forest's asking price, which could potentially impact the deal. Manchester United are also interested in signing Anderson, but it appears that Manchester City are currently in the driving seat. A record transfer fee is being discussed, with negotiations ongoing between the clubs.

stories.headline: The French Open is currently underway. Here we take a look at French Open stats throughout the years and who dominates the clay the most.
stories.summary: The French Open 2026 is currently underway at Roland-Garros. Rafael Nadal holds the record for the most Men's Singles titles with 14 wins. In the women's singles, Iga Swiatek has dominated the clay court, making at least the semifinal in four straight French Opens and winning four of the past six. Other top contenders include Novak Djokovic, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander Zverev, who is considered one of the best clay-court players. In the women's singles, Coco Gauff is also chasing clay greatness. The tournament features a strong field of players, with matches, scores, and results available to follow. The event can be watched live, with a schedule of upcoming matches and stars to watch. The French Open 2026 continues, with players competing for the top prize on the clay courts of Roland-Garros.

stories.headline: Star forward Ryan Oosthuizen believes a desire to match his double RWC-winning compatriots will ensure there is no let up as South Africa seek more glory in Val
stories.summary: South Africa's Blitzboks won their second title of the 2025-26 series, defeating Fiji 21-19 in the final at HBF Park in Perth. Veteran forward Ryan Oosthuizen starred in the final, scoring two tries, and rated the win as one of the best of his career. The victory comes after the team's fourth-place finish in Singapore, and Oosthuizen attributed the success to the team's ability to hold themselves to a high standard. The win marks the Blitzboks' second title of the series, following their victory in Cape Town in December. Oosthuizen's performance earned him the Player of the Final award, and he believes the team is heading in the right direction to become the best sevens team in the world. The Blitzboks' win in Perth is a significant milestone in their quest for glory.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu political crisis: Rebel AIADMK MLA Balakrishna Reddy backs EPS, submits apology letter amid party turmoil
stories.summary: Rebel AIADMK MLA Balakrishna Reddy has submitted an apology letter to the Speaker's office, expressing support for the EPS faction led by Palaniswami. This move comes amid growing factionalism within the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. Reddy's apology is an attempt to avoid disqualification, following a series of resignations by rebel legislators. Five other AIADMK MLAs had submitted similar apology letters a day earlier, also backing the Palaniswami faction. The AIADMK is facing an internal crisis after its poor performance in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, where it won 47 seats, behind TVK's 108 and the DMK's 59. The party is divided, with rival factions backing different leaders and questioning EPS' leadership. The development is a significant shift in the party's dynamics, as Reddy had earlier backed the TVK-led government during the floor test.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to rule today on whether Election Commission crossed the line over SIR
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is set to rule on the constitutional validity of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The challenge questions whether the ECI has the authority to undertake a de novo reconstruction of electoral rolls. The petitioners argue that the ECI crossed its limits in doing so. The case has been heard by a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, who will pronounce the verdict. The ECI had faced questions from the court for not citing illegal immigration as a reason for its actions. The ruling will determine whether the ECI's actions were within its constitutional powers. The verdict is highly anticipated, as it will have implications for the Election Commission's authority and the integrity of the electoral process in India. The court's decision is expected to be announced today.

stories.headline: BREAKING| Supreme Court To Pronounce Judgment Tomorrow On Legality Of SIR Carried Out By Election Commission Of India
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India will pronounce judgment on the legality of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls carried out by the Election Commission of India. The court will deliver its verdict on a batch of petitions challenging the constitutional validity of the SIR exercise. The SIR process involves door-to-door verification by electoral officials to update electoral rolls. The judgment is expected to address concerns surrounding the legitimacy of the SIR process. The Election Commission of India had conducted the SIR to ensure accurate and up-to-date electoral rolls, particularly in West Bengal. The court's decision will provide clarity on the matter, which has been a subject of controversy and petitions seeking its legality to be examined. The judgment is scheduled to be pronounced tomorrow.

stories.headline: Passengers evacuated using slides at BLR after smoke on taxiing IndiGo aircraft
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A321neo was evacuated at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport after smoke was detected in the cabin while taxiing. The flight, 6E 6017, was bound for Chennai with over 230 passengers and crew members on board. Emergency slides were used to evacuate everyone safely to the terminal. Two passengers were injured during the evacuation. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening while the aircraft was preparing for departure. The airline ensured the comfort and well-being of all passengers and crew after the evacuation. The cause of the smoke is not specified, but the swift evacuation prevented any further harm. All passengers and crew were safely moved off the aircraft, and the airline is likely to investigate the incident.

stories.headline: Iceland Mulls Joining EU as Arctic Tensions Rise
stories.summary: Iceland is considering joining the European Union as tensions rise in the Arctic region. The country, a close EU partner but not a full member, is split on the issue, with polls showing a divided population. A referendum is set to take place in less than 100 days, where voters will decide whether to restart EU membership talks, which were halted over a decade ago. The government may bring forward the referendum due to deteriorating ties with the US. Iceland's prime minister, Katrín Jakobsdóttir, notes that foreign policy now occupies a more important place in voters' minds, citing the "Greenland crisis" as a factor. The vote will not determine immediate EU membership, but rather whether accession talks should be restarted, potentially offering the EU a strategic foothold in the Arctic region.

stories.headline: Varcoe: Alberta's new finance minister won't open spending floodgates
stories.summary: Alberta's new finance minister is preparing an economic recovery package to address a looming recession, with costs expected to exceed $3 billion. The package aims to stimulate the economy and mitigate the impact of the recession. Despite the significant spending, the finance minister has indicated that they will not open the spending floodgates, suggesting a balanced approach to managing the province's finances. The economic recovery package is expected to be announced soon, with details on the specific measures and funding allocations to be revealed. The package is part of a broader effort to support Alberta's economy during a challenging period, and its success will be closely watched by businesses, investors, and residents alike. The province's fiscal management will be crucial in navigating the economic downturn.

stories.headline: Aberdeen's Glover: Space, capital and the long view
stories.summary: Aberdeen's Kevin Glover has written about the opportunities in space, noting it reaches beyond geopolitics and science policy. His comments were part of a discussion on space, capital, and long-term views. In related news, Aberdeen has seen developments in its city, including a major residential-led transformation of a former department store on Union Street. Meanwhile, delegates from Aberdeen, South Dakota, visited Pittsburg after a nationwide search, choosing the city for its potential. Glover's views on space highlight its potential for investment and growth, with open-ended funds being considered. His comments were published on multiple occasions, including April 29 and January 27, with the most recent publication being May 26, 2026. The discussions and developments showcase Aberdeen's involvement in various sectors, including space, investments, and urban transformation.

News anchors have been observed using identical phrases when reporting on certain topics, such as attacks on Trump. stories.headline: Stock Market Highlights, May 26: Sensex falls 479 points, Nifty slips below 23,950 as rupee weakens
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty closed significantly lower on May 26. The Sensex fell 479 points, while the Nifty slipped below 23,950. The decline was largely due to a downturn in banking, oil and gas, and pharma stocks. The rupee's weakness also contributed to the market's poor performance. The Sensex had opened over 130 points lower and briefly turned positive before slipping back into the red. It ultimately fell 600 points from its day's high. In contrast, small and midcap stocks performed well. The market's decline was a reversal from earlier gains, with the Nifty ending near the psychologically important 23,900-mark. The downturn was widespread, with key sectors contributing to the losses. Overall, the Indian stock market closed in the red on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty opens red on geopolitical tensions, FII outflows
stories.summary: The Indian stock market opened in the red due to geopolitical tensions and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) outflows. The Sensex and Nifty50 indices declined, following a day of volatile trading on weak global sentiment. The US launch of fresh strikes in Iran and rising crude prices have contributed to the market downturn. The Sensex was down at 76,009.7, while the Nifty 50 settled at 23,913.7, with losses of 0.49 percent. Global markets, including the Stoxx Europe 600, also fell. The decline is attributed to various factors, including the Iran-US conflict, oil prices soaring above $100/barrel, a falling rupee, rising bond yields, profit booking, and persistent FII outflows. The market volatility has left investors puzzled, with analysts citing geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties as key factors.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty open flat as Middle East tensions keep investors cautious
stories.summary: Benchmark stock market indices, Sensex and Nifty, opened flat on Wednesday due to cautious investor sentiment. The fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran, along with rising crude oil prices and global tensions, contributed to the cautious tone. Earlier, GIFT Nifty had indicated a positive opening, but investor concerns prevailed. This follows a sharp decline in Indian stock markets on March 15, 2026, when the Sensex crashed 516 points due to renewed US-Iran tensions. In contrast, stocks had surged on April 8, 2026, with the Sensex gaining 2800 points as crude oil prices declined. However, rising crude prices and Middle East tensions have since weighed on the markets, affecting investor sentiment and leading to a flat opening on Wednesday. Elevated crude oil prices continue to impact market performance.

stories.headline: Nvidia has a $200 Billion Warning for AMD and Intel Stock Investors
stories.summary: Nvidia's Vera CPU is opening a new $200 billion Total Addressable Market (TAM) for the company, a market it has not previously addressed. This development is expected to bring in nearly $20 billion in total CPU revenue for Nvidia. The company's entry into this new market is seen as a warning for AMD and Intel stock investors, as it potentially threatens their market share. Major hyperscale and system makers are partnering with Nvidia, further solidifying its position. Recently, Nvidia bought back $2 billion in stock during the current quarter, and the company has $5 billion available for repurchases. The Vera CPU represents a significant expansion of Nvidia's business, and its impact on the market is being closely watched by investors and industry observers. Nvidia's move into this new market is a notable development in the tech industry.

stories.headline: CFTC issued approvals to three prediction market companies with ties to the Trumps - report
stories.summary: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has issued approvals to three prediction market companies, including Crypto.com, Polymarket, and a Gemini offshoot tied to the Trump family. This move comes amid layoffs and sidelined investigators. The CFTC has been taking a stance against states trying to regulate prediction markets, with the agency stating "we will see you in court." The approved companies have ties to the Trump family, sparking interest in the regulatory decisions. The CFTC has also been active in enforcing trading regulations, recently ordering two trading firms and a bank to pay $3 million for spoofing. The agency's actions are being closely watched, particularly in relation to its handling of prediction markets and companies connected to the Trump family.

stories.headline: $10.2M Talc Verdict Names Maker of Target, Walmart Store Brands
stories.summary: A Ramsey County jury has awarded $10.2 million to a local man who developed mesothelioma after using asbestos-contaminated talc products. The verdict names several companies responsible, including Vi-Jon LLC, maker of store brands for Walmart, Target, and Walgreens, as well as Sanofi, Merck, Johnson & Johnson, and Perrigo Co. of Tennessee. The man used store-brand body, baby, and foot powders for decades, including Walmart's Equate, Target's Up & Up, and Walgreens-branded products, all manufactured by Vi-Jon LLC. The finding highlights the widespread risk of asbestos-contaminated talc in numerous products on store shelves nationwide. This verdict is believed to be the second-largest mesothelioma personal injury award in Minnesota history, holding significant importance for retailers who lend their brand names to third-party manufactured products. The companies were found responsible for the man's condition due to their use of asbestos-contaminated talc.

stories.headline: Some of Texas' most famous BBQ joints forced to close due to sky-high beef prices
stories.summary: Texas BBQ joints are struggling due to sky-high beef prices, with some being forced to close. Ground beef prices have increased over 15% from last year, and wholesale brisket costs $5 to $6 per pound before smoking, trimming, and labor. As a result, some restaurants are charging $35 to $40 per pound to stay afloat. BBQ joint owners in Texas have been in "survival mode" for a year, fighting to stay open amid the high prices. Russell Roegels, owner of two Houston BBQ restaurants, described the situation as "as bad as it gets." The rising beef prices are threatening the iconic Texas brisket boom, forcing owners to consider raising prices, changing menus, or shutting down. The historic highs in beef prices are having a significant impact on Texas BBQ restaurants, with some owners struggling to keep their businesses open.

stories.headline: Critics say Pope Leo's 'AI encyclical' fails to grapple with AI's real challenges Pope Leo's 'AI encyclical' wants AI to serve humanity, not be disempowered by it. Achieving that vision will be tough.
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has released his first encyclical on artificial intelligence, "Magnifica humanitas," marking the 135th anniversary of Rerum novarum. The document emphasizes that AI must serve humanity, not concentrate power. However, critics argue that the encyclical fails to adequately address the real challenges posed by AI. The pope warns of the risks of control over digital space shifting to for-profit entities and emphasizes the importance of humane labor practices and just wages. He also acknowledges that AI is fundamentally not human and cannot take away human dignity. The encyclical is part of the pope's ongoing efforts to address the implications of AI on humanity, which he has emphasized since becoming pope. Achieving the vision of AI serving humanity will be a difficult task, requiring careful consideration of the complex issues involved.

stories.headline: OpenAI Sam Altman dismisses fears of AI-driven job losses SYDNEY, Australia: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman has said that rapid adoption of artificial intelligence will not lead to
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has dismissed fears of AI-driven job losses, stating that rapid adoption of artificial intelligence will not lead to widespread unemployment. Speaking at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia's technology conference in Sydney, Altman expressed his belief that many jobs will continue to require human communication, mitigating the impact of AI on employment. This statement comes as a reversal of his previous stance on the issue, with Altman admitting he was wrong about AI's impact on jobs. The OpenAI chief's comments aim to alleviate concerns about the potential job apocalypse fueled by artificial intelligence, highlighting the importance of human skills in the workforce. Altman's remarks were made during a virtual appearance at the conference, where he shared his updated perspective on the intersection of AI and employment.

stories.headline: OpenAI boss: artificial intelligence won’t create jobs apocalypse Sam Altman admitted he had overestimated the social and economic impacts of AI in 2022 but the size of the blow to the labour market remains unclear
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated that artificial intelligence will not lead to a "jobs apocalypse" as previously predicted. Speaking at a Commonwealth Bank of Australia conference in Sydney, Altman admitted that his earlier estimates of the social and economic impact of AI were incorrect. He acknowledged that while OpenAI's technology predictions following the launch of ChatGPT in 2022 were broadly correct, the impact on the job market was overstated. Altman believes that human interaction will always be needed, mitigating the potential negative effects of AI on employment. He clarified that the size of the blow to the labour market remains unclear, but expressed confidence that the outcome will not be as severe as initially thought. Altman's revised assessment suggests a more nuanced understanding of AI's role in the job market.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Sam Altman says artificial intelligence unlikely to lead to 'jobs apocalypse' Altman said he and his executives had been roughly right on the technological predictions made by OpenAI when it launched ChatGPT in 2022. But he said they were
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated that the rapid development and adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) will not lead to a global "jobs apocalypse". He admitted that his initial fears about white-collar job losses due to AI were exaggerated. Altman noted that the technology has not claimed as many white-collar jobs as he had anticipated. He attributed this to the irreplaceable human element in many jobs, suggesting that the future job market will be different than initially predicted. Altman made these comments after reflecting on the technological predictions made by OpenAI when it launched ChatGPT in 2022, stating that he and his executives were "roughly right" in their predictions. The impact of AI on jobs has been less severe than feared, according to Altman. He believes AI will bring changes to the job market, but not a catastrophic "jobs apocalypse".
